title: Delivered mobile radars turn allied air-surveillance procurement into an integrated capability stage
source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of AN/TPS-77 MRR radar delivery and integration
geography: Lithuania and NATO integrated air and missile defence system

denominator.unit: named Lithuanian airspace-surveillance capability route using AN/TPS-77 MRR mobile medium-range radars

delivery_status.value: radars manufactured by Lockheed Martin were reported delivered to Lithuania

integration_status.value: Lithuanian Armed Forces were reported to be deploying the radars and connecting real-time data to NATO's integrated air and missile defence system

claimed_capability.value: timely airborne-object detection, more flexible surveillance, contribution to the common Alliance air picture, and improved Lithuanian-allied interoperability

follow_on_contracts.value: additional contracts were stated as planned for 2026 to strengthen recognition and neutralization of air threats

operational_effect.unit: missing quantity, acceptance record, uptime, training, actual detections, response outcomes, readiness, deterrence, and civilian-protection effect

mechanism.value: A delivered sensor becomes strategically consequential only through integration, staffing, availability, data-sharing, and response; delivery and declared interoperability establish a stronger capability stage without proving operational effect.

observations.method: Structured extraction from the Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence announcement. Delivery, integration, claimed surveillance function, and planned follow-on procurement are kept separate from acceptance, availability, actual detection, response, deterrence, and civilian outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The announcement does not publish contract value, number of radars, acceptance documentation, deployment locations, training or staffing, network performance, uptime, detection records, response timing, or later airspace outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Lithuanian Armed Forces, NATO air-defence partners, Lockheed Martin, and populations exposed to Baltic airspace risk; no civilian or operational-outcome subgroup is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: Delivered and integrated sensors may improve shared awareness and allied coordination, while capability claims can still overstate readiness if staffing, network availability, response assets, or maintenance are constrained.

related_sources.claim: NATO Baltic Air Policing provides the allied air-policing context in which national surveillance and shared air-picture integration operate.
A same-day Lithuanian defense-industrial funding announcement provides a separate production-capacity stage; it is not evidence of radar delivery or operation.

boundary: This record establishes reported delivery and integration of AN/TPS-77 MRR radars into Lithuanian/NATO air-surveillance arrangements, plus a stated follow-on procurement plan. It does not establish acceptance, sustained availability, actual detections, response outcomes, deterrence, reduced civilian risk, or public consent.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project follow-up memo derived from the official Lithuanian Ministry source; contract files, operational logs, and civilian incident records are not retained.
